newsitem.title: USA: Boston Redevelopment Authority head quits - report.
newsitem.headline: Boston Redevelopment Authority head quits - report.

text.p: Boston Redevelopment Authority director Marisa Lago has resigned under pressure from Mayor Thomas Menino, the Boston Herald reported Thursday.
Lago took a $98,000-a-year job as head of international relations for the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington, the newspaper said.
Paul McCann, a veteran authority manager, was named Lago's temporary successor.
Lago had been under pressure from City Hall to leave for months after a series of snubs by the mayor and his top aides left her a minor player, the newspaper said.

The resignation comes at a time when Menino is weeks away from launching his reelection bid and confronts a complex stadium and convention center proposal and a controversial plan to build a mall over the Massachusetts Turnpike.
Authority officials and a spokesman for the mayor were not immediately available.
